title: Learning: Insight Learning, Social Learning, Latent Learning
summary: Insight learning (Wolfgang Köhler); social learning theory (Albert Bandura); latent learning; cognitive map; observational learning.
objectives: Explain latent learning and cognitive map.
revision: Insight learning = sudden problem solution (Köhler's chimpanzee with sticks). Social learning = observation/imitation (Bandura). Latent learning = learning without reinforcement (Tolman's cognitive map). Observational learning = watching models (vicarious reinforcement).
traps: Latent learning = learning without reinforcement, shown later.
confusions: Confusing insight learning with trial-and-error learning.
Believing latent learning requires reinforcement during learning.

notes.t: Wolfgang Köhler demonstrated insight learning with chimpanzees who suddenly solved problems (e.g., using sticks to reach bananas) through sudden understanding rather than gradual trial-and-error.
Albert Bandura's social learning theory proposes that people learn by observing others (models), through observation, imitation, and modeling.
Latent learning: learning that occurs without immediate reinforcement and is not demonstrated until reinforcement is provided.
A cognitive map is a mental representation of the spatial layout of an environment, demonstrated in Tolman's rat experiments.
Observational learning: learning by watching others' behavior and its consequences (vicarious reinforcement).
UGC NET frequently asks about Köhler's insight learning, Bandura's social learning theory, and Tolman's cognitive map.

mnemonics.title: ISLO
mnemonics.text: I — Insight learning (Köhler, sudden understanding), S — Social learning (Bandura, observation), L — Latent learning (Tolman, learning without reinforcement), O — Observational learning (watching models)
